title: Chapter 11 Quiz: Deployment & Security
description: Test your knowledge of deploying Django apps and securing them.

questions.question: Which setting must be set to `False` in production?
questions.explanation: `DEBUG` must be `False` in production to avoid exposing sensitive information.

questions.question: It is safe to leave `DEBUG = True` in production if you restrict access by IP.
questions.explanation: False. `DEBUG = True` can still expose sensitive data in error pages, even with IP restrictions.

questions.question: What does `collectstatic` do?
options: Collects all static files into a single directory
questions.explanation: It copies static files from apps and `STATICFILES_DIRS` to `STATIC_ROOT`.

questions.question: To serve static files with Whitenoise, you must add `whitenoise.middleware.WhiteNoiseMiddleware` to the `______` list.
questions.explanation: Whitenoise middleware is added to the `MIDDLEWARE` list, usually after SecurityMiddleware.

questions.question: Which of the following is a production‑ready web server for Django?
questions.explanation: Gunicorn is a production WSGI server; `runserver` is only for development.

questions.question: Environment variables are a secure way to store secrets because they are not stored in version control.
questions.explanation: True. Environment variables are injected at runtime and not committed to code repositories.

questions.question: Which setting prevents your site from being embedded in an iframe?
questions.explanation: `X_FRAME_OPTIONS = 'DENY'` prevents clickjacking.

questions.question: To enforce HTTPS, set `SECURE_SSL_______ = True`.
questions.explanation: `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True` redirects HTTP to HTTPS.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` setting?
options: To limit which domains can access the site
To set allowed IP addresses for the admin
To specify which hosts can serve static files
questions.explanation: `ALLOWED_HOSTS` is a list of domain names that Django will accept requests from, preventing HTTP Host header attacks.

questions.question: Using `django-environ` can automatically parse a `DATABASE_URL` into a `DATABASES` dictionary.
questions.explanation: True. `django-environ` provides `db_url()` to convert a URL into a database config.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Django built‑in security feature?
questions.explanation: Django does not automatically rotate passwords; that's handled by user action or extensions.

questions.question: The `SECRET_KEY` is used to sign cookies and other data. It must be kept ______.
questions.explanation: If the secret key is exposed, attackers can forge signed data.

questions.question: What does `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS` do?
options: Forces browsers to only use HTTPS for the specified number of seconds
questions.explanation: HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) instructs browsers to always use HTTPS for the domain.

questions.question: You should commit your `.env` file to version control so that other developers can use it.
questions.explanation: False. `.env` contains secrets and should be added to `.gitignore`.

questions.question: Which command would you run to see all pending migrations before deploying?
questions.explanation: `showmigrations` lists applied and unapplied migrations.

questions.question: To serve media files in production, you typically configure your web server to serve from the ______ directory.
questions.explanation: `MEDIA_ROOT` is the absolute filesystem path for user‑uploaded files.

questions.question: Which of the following is a recommended practice for handling user‑uploaded files?
options: Store them in the project directory
Use a cloud storage service like S3
Allow users to specify file paths
questions.explanation: Cloud storage is scalable and offloads serving from your application servers.

questions.question: Django automatically protects against SQL injection when using raw SQL queries.
questions.explanation: False. When using `raw()` or `execute()`, you must manually parameterize queries to avoid injection.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE`?
options: To ensure the CSRF cookie is only sent over HTTPS
To set the CSRF cookie as HttpOnly
To set the CSRF token expiration
questions.explanation: `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True` transmits the CSRF cookie only over HTTPS.

questions.question: In a production environment, you should run `collectstatic` and then restart the web server to serve updated static files. The command to collect static files is `python manage.py ______`.
questions.explanation: `collectstatic` gathers static files into `STATIC_ROOT`.
